samples.summary: Test named "does not crash when a callback arrives before anyone awaits it" never exercises a rejection, so it cannot fail if the `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` guard is removed
samples.evidence: The test hits `/callback?code=unbound` with no `state`. In login.ts:306-317 that branch writes a 400 and returns — it never calls `callbackReject`, and `settled` stays false. The only path that rejects `callbackPromise` is the 30s timeout (login.ts:373-385), which this test never triggers (it waits 50 ms and asserts the promise is still pending). So the pre-attached `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` added at login.ts:259 — the whole behavior the test's comment claims to protect ("a rejection raised in that window must not surface as an unhandled rejection") — is never exercised. Deleting line 259 leaves this test green. There are no fake timers anywhere in the file (no `vi.useFakeTimers`), so no other test covers it either.

samples.summary: No test covers the `login` action body: nonce minting, `--allow-unbound-callback` wiring into `startCallbackServer`, or that `open()`/stderr receive `startUrl` rather than the nonce-carrying authorize URL
samples.evidence: The only test of the command is `registerLoginCommand` → `expect(login?.options.map(o => o.long)).toContain('--allow-unbound-callback')`, which asserts the option exists but nothing about its effect. The action (login.ts:22-83) is where `randomBytes(32)` is minted, `allowUnbound: localOpts.allowUnboundCallback === true` is passed, `setAuthorizeUrl(buildAuthorizeUrl(...))` is called and `open(startUrl)`/`console.error(startUrl)` happen. If the action passed `state` to `open()` (the leak this change exists to prevent), or wired the flag to the wrong option name (commander camel-casing), every test in the file would still pass, because they all call `startCallbackServer`/`buildAuthorizeUrl` directly with hand-built arguments. Searched packages/cli/test for `allowUnbound`, `open(`, `startUrl` — only helper-level uses.

samples.summary: The changed timeout behavior — reporting UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE instead of the generic timeout when only nonce-less callbacks were seen — has no test

finding.summary: Test named "does not crash when a callback arrives before anyone awaits it" never exercises a rejection, so it cannot fail if the `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` guard is removed
finding.evidence: The test hits `/callback?code=unbound` with no `state`. In login.ts:306-317 that branch writes a 400 and returns — it never calls `callbackReject`, and `settled` stays false. The only path that rejects `callbackPromise` is the 30s timeout (login.ts:373-385), which this test never triggers (it waits 50 ms and asserts the promise is still pending). So the pre-attached `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` added at login.ts:259 — the whole behavior the test's comment claims to protect ("a rejection raised in that window must not surface as an unhandled rejection") — is never exercised. Deleting line 259 leaves this test green. There are no fake timers anywhere in the file (no `vi.useFakeTimers`), so no other test covers it either.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out. The test at login-callback.test.ts:121-134 issues GET /callback?code=unbound, which lands in the no-state branch at login.ts:306-317 that writes 400 and returns without touching `settled` or calling `callbackReject`. The sole rejection path is the 30s timeout at login.ts:373-385, which the test never reaches — it waits 50ms and then close() (login.ts:404-407) clears the timeout. Therefore the `callbackPromise.catch(() => {})` guard at login.ts:259, which the test's own comment says it protects ("a rejection raised in that window must not surface as an unhandled rejection"), is never exercised; removing line 259 leaves the test passing. Its two assertions are also a subset of the preceding test at login-callback.test.ts:92-119. A repo-wide grep for useFakeTimers/advanceTimersBy/30_000/30000 in packages/cli yields only docs-export.test.ts:184 (a test-timeout arg) and the production setTimeout, and startCallbackServer/waitForCallback appear in no other file, so no other test drives the rejection either. This is fake coverage for a named behavior with no meaningful test anywhere — squarely in the test-adequacy lane and major.

verdict.reason: No counterexample exists. The login action body (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:22-83) is never invoked by any test: repo-wide greps for `registerLoginCommand`, `allowUnboundCallback`, `startCallbackServer`, `setAuthorizeUrl`, `startUrl`, and any mock/import of the `open` module (zero matches anywhere outside login.ts itself) turn up only helper-level usage inside packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts, where every server is built by hand with a locally minted NONCE and an explicit options object. finding.summary: Test 'does not crash when a callback arrives before anyone awaits it' cannot fail — the path it claims to cover no longer rejects
finding.evidence: The test drives `/callback?code=unbound` and asserts a 400 plus that the promise has not settled. But after this delta the nonce-less branch (src/commands/login.ts:306-317) never calls `callbackReject` — it only warns and returns. The only remaining rejection path is the 30s timeout, which the test never reaches. So the guard the test exists to protect (`callbackPromise.catch(() => {})`, login.ts:259) could be deleted entirely and this test would still pass; it is now an exact duplicate of the assertions in the preceding test at line 92. To be meaningful it would have to trigger an actual pre-await rejection (e.g. an injectable/faked timeout) and assert no unhandled rejection occurred.

verdict.reason: Verified against the repository; the finding holds as described. (1) The nonce-less branch at packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:306-317 writes 400, warns once, and returns — it never calls callbackReject; the surrounding comment (299-305) says this is intentional. (2) The only callbackReject call site in the file is inside the 30_000 ms setTimeout at login.ts:373-385. (3) The test 'does not crash when a callback arrives before anyone awaits it' (packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:121-134) issues /callback?code=unbound, asserts status 400, then races waitForCallback() for only 50 ms via settledWithin (defined at test:29-38) and calls srv.close() in the finally, which clears that 30 s timer (login.ts:404-407). The callback promise therefore never rejects during the test, so the guard it claims to protect (callbackPromise.catch(() => {}) at login.ts:259) could be deleted and both assertions would still pass — they are true regardless of whether the guard works. The assertions are also a strict subset of the preceding test at test:98-105, which drives the same request and asserts the same 400 plus non-settlement. There is no seam to trigger a real pre-await rejection (startCallbackServer options are only { allowUnbound?, warn? } at login.ts:234) and the test registers no unhandled-rejection listener. This is a vacuous test presented as coverage for a specific guard — squarely in the test-adequacy lane and major by the rubric.

verdict.reason: The branch exists as described: login.ts:373-385 rejects with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE instead of 'Login timed out...' when sawUnboundCallback is true, on a hardcoded 30_000ms setTimeout. startCallbackServer's options (login.ts:232-234) expose only allowUnbound and warn, so there is no timeout seam. The sole test file touching this code is packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts (repo-wide grep for startCallbackServer returns only it and login.ts); it asserts UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE only as an HTTP response body (line 100) and asserts the warning does NOT mention --allow-unbound-callback (line 104). No fake timers exist anywhere in packages/cli (vi.useFakeTimers hits only in slides/frontend/backend), and packages/cli/vitest.config.ts declares no setup file or global fakeTimers. No other CLI test, e2e harness, or helper exercises the login flow. So the timeout message selection — the only real-run signal of server version skew — ships with no meaningful test and is unreachable from the suite as written.

searchedFor: grep for mocks of 'open' in packages/cli/test
glob packages/cli/test/** for a login action test
finding.summary: No test covers login.ts's actual hand-off: that `open()` and stderr receive `startUrl` and not the nonce-bearing URL
finding.evidence: The test titled 'keeps the nonce out of the URL handed to the browser and to stderr' (test line 184) only inspects the `startUrl` string returned by `startCallbackServer` and the `/start` redirect. It never touches the login action handler, so the security property it names — login.ts:66-72 printing `startUrl` and passing `startUrl` (not `buildAuthorizeUrl(...)`) to `open()` — is untested: swapping line 67 or line 72 back to the nonce-carrying URL would break the stated guarantee with every test still green. The only test of the action-registering function (test line 226) asserts merely that the command and the `--allow-unbound-callback` option exist, which says nothing about the hand-off.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: login.ts's browser hand-off (login.ts:66-72 — print `startUrl`, `open(startUrl)`) lives inside the `.action()` closure of `registerLoginCommand`, and no test in the repository invokes that closure. The test at login-callback.test.ts:184 that is named for this exact property ("keeps the nonce out of the URL handed to the browser and to stderr") only drives `startCallbackServer` directly: it calls `setAuthorizeUrl` itself, asserts `srv.startUrl` equals `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start` and that `/start` 302s to the nonce URL. It never stubs `open`, never captures stderr, never runs the action. The only `registerLoginCommand` test (line 226) asserts the command name and `--allow-unbound-callback` option exist. I searched wide for a counterexample: repo-wide grep for `startUrl|setAuthorizeUrl|buildAuthorizeUrl` hits only login.ts, that one test file, and a .agent-review artifact; grep for `registerLoginCommand|commands/login|Opening browser|allow-unbound-callback` hits only login.ts, cli.ts, that test, and docs; no test anywhere mocks the `open` module; all `**/*.{test,spec}.*` files and every test/tests/e2e/__tests__ directory mentioning "login" resolve to incidental string matches (cli/output.test.ts:504, cli/schema.test.ts:46,66,75,91, cli/url.test.ts:43) or the backend GitHub strategy spec; bin.test.ts mocks `runCli` so there is no CLI-spawning e2e path. Swapping login.ts:67 or :72 to `buildAuthorizeUrl(server, port, state)` would break the stated guarantee with the entire suite still green. Real and blocking: a security-relevant behavior change whose only nominally-covering test does not exercise the code path.
